name: Google BigQuery
model: Tables of typed columns (nested and repeated fields allowed), GoogleSQL; serverless data warehouse billed per bytes scanned or slots
engine_note: Capacitor columnar files on Colossus storage, queried by Dremel workers; storage and compute fully separated
consistency: Multi-statement, multi-table transactions (up to 100 tables, across datasets and projects) with snapshot isolation. Two transactions mutating the same table conflict and one is cancelled; reads and appends run alongside. Single-statement DML is atomic.
scaling: Serverless: compute (slots) and storage scale separately and automatically; you pay on-demand per TB scanned or reserve slot capacity.
version_note: Release notes 2026-10-02: Rust SDK for BigQuery generally available.
reach: Reach for it when your data already lives in Google Cloud and you want ad hoc SQL over terabytes with no servers or cluster sizing.
avoid: Avoid for app reads and writes per request: queries take seconds, DML is rate limited, and careless SELECT * over big tables costs money.
escape: terabyte-scale analytics with no cluster to size; Postgres would need a large box and still scan rows
chat: Warehouse copy of all chats, messages and usage events for company-wide analytics and finance.
notes: Consistency from the transactions page (fetched 2026-10-04; cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs now redirects to docs.cloud.google.com). 'Capacitor', 'Colossus', 'Dremel' names are from Google's storage overview and published Dremel papers, not re-fetched in this pass; treat as well known but not re-checked today.
